title: AI Engineering at Jane Street - John Crepezzi
summary: Jane Street describes training custom models for OCaml using workspace-snapshot data, RL against build and test results, and a shared editor backend.

assertions.quote: models themselves are just not very good at oaml

verdicts.note: Model quality tracks training-data volume; benchmarks such as MultiPL-E show much lower scores in less common languages.

assertions.quote: you have to have the model see a bunch of examples that are in the shape of the type of question

verdicts.note: Supervised fine-tuning works best when training data matches the deployment input/output format, consistent with Meta's CodeCompose and general fine-tuning experience.

assertions.quote: better align the model to write code that actually does compile and past tests

verdicts.note: RL with verifiable rewards from execution and tests is a well-established technique behind recent coding model gains.

assertions.quote: having evaluations that are meaningful is kind of a Cornerstone of making sure that models don't go off the rails

verdicts.note: Without task-level evals, fine-tuning regressions go unnoticed; this is standard ML practice.

assertions.quote: we're able to change it in one place Downstream of the editors and then have it available everywhere

verdicts.note: Decoupling tooling from a single model eases switching, which matters given fast model turnover, but it is an architecture choice with tradeoffs rather than a measured result.
